title: Gas Clothes Dryer Installation: Piping, Venting, and Commissioning (This Old House)

locations.name: Basement
locations.basis: Explicit mentions of the basement throughout the transcript (e.g., 'the basement,' 'we'll head down to the basement').

summary: This Old House guides a family through installing a gas clothes dryer in their basement, covering site assessment, electrical and gas feasibility, gas piping installation, venting to the exterior, and final commissioning. The episode contrasts electric versus gas dryer options, stresses the need to verify electrical service (panel capacity) and gas availability, and demonstrates practical piping techniques (black steel pipe, pipe dope, threaded joints), venting details (exterior termination with louvers), and connection methods (unions or flexible connectors) before performing a leak test and turning the gas back on. The host also notes safety considerations, including that gas piping should be done by a licensed professional, and closes with a personal update on the family.
topics: Threaded fittings and tightening procedures (two-wrench method)
Vent piping to exterior and termination louvers
Exterior vent protection and bird prevention
Unions and stainless steel flexible connectors
Electrical requirements for dryers (110V plug) and panel capacity (60A vs 200A)
Gas line availability and feasibility in a typical home
Safety considerations and licensing for gas work

sections.title: Project scope and site readiness
sections.description: Introduction to the family's laundry needs, existing washer hookup in the basement, and the initial assessment of space, venting options, and electrical capacity guiding the dryer choice.

sections.title: Electric vs. gas dryer feasibility and gas line availability
sections.description: Discussion of electrical load versus a potential gas option, including the panel size and the presence of a gas line, which influence whether a gas dryer is a viable, more powerful alternative.

sections.title: Gas piping installation
sections.description: Setup of the gas piping run: selecting pipe length, threading joints, applying thread sealant, tightening with wrenches, and preparing a vertical drop with a drip cap for future cleaning.

sections.title: Venting, termination, and connector options
sections.description: Installation of the vent path to the outside, including the exterior termination and clamps, and discussion of how to join the vent to the dryer using either a union or a flexible connector for proper alignment.

sections.title: Final test, commissioning, and wrap-up
sections.description: Completion steps including leak testing after connections, turning the gas back on, and wrapping up with observational notes and a family update.

featured_techniques.technique: Gas piping installation using black steel pipe
Applying pipe thread sealant (pipe dope) and tightening threaded joints with two wrenches
Vent piping termination with exterior louvers and securing clamps
Using a union or flexible connector to join vent/piping to the appliance
Gas leak testing and commissioning after piping installation
Electrical capacity evaluation for dryer installation (panel considerations for 60A vs. 200A systems)
Safety note: gas piping should be performed by a licensed professional
